They're not the same. HTTP/1.1 keep-alive only reuses the TCP connection, but requests still go one at a time per connection, so a slow response blocks the ones behind it and browsers work around that by opening several connections. HTTP/2 multiplexes many concurrent request/response streams over a single connection with binary framing and header compression, so there's no application-level head-of-line blocking (TCP-level blocking can still happen).

`as const` changes the inferred type (literals stay literal and everything becomes readonly) and checks nothing. `satisfies` checks a value against a type without changing its inferred type, so you catch typos and missing keys and keep the precise type. You can combine them: `as const satisfies Config` gives a checked, literal, readonly value.

A Deployment treats pods as interchangeable and disposable: any pod can be replaced or rescheduled, names are random and storage is shared or absent. A StatefulSet gives each pod a stable identity (ordinal name like db-0, stable DNS) and its own persistent volume, with ordered startup and shutdown. Pick it for things like databases, Kafka or ZooKeeper where each replica needs its own durable state or fixed identity.
